en: *sniff* Dad...
A child's got to leave their parents' protection eventually. That's why I don't fault ya for what you're doin'.
It's only when you take your first step out of the nest that you realize your parents were guarding you with everything they got.
...Yeah.
Hey, ya couldn't stay in town bein' a child, Masao. Ya had it right on that one. But now, you gotta make good on that conviction. Start walkin' on yer own two feet.
You're right. I... I needed to be set straight. My parents paying my debt, and you defending me from those guys... I get it now. I need to actually step into true independence.
Thank you, Saejima-san. I'm going to try harder, and truly be worthy of my father's pride.
Sounds good. Take care, Masao. You'll be fine.
That means a lot. Goodbye!
(Yeah, he's a good kid. Never give up, Masao...)
Uh... I beg your pardon, but is that you, Saejima-san?
It's me, Masao! We met in my village!
Masao! Wasn't expectin' to run into ya here.
I'm as surprised as you are. When did you get to Tsukimino?
Short time ago. Heard ya became a host. I went by yer club.
Oh? Really? Did they say anything about me?
Tch, yeah. They said they're gonna track ya down. Ran out owin' 300,000 yen, did ya?
I... That was a setup! I had no idea what was going on, and suddenly I owed all this money...
Yeah, I know their dirty tricks. But you were naive as hell, too. Thought you could make easy money bein' a host, did ya?
A bumpkin like you is a ready-made victim for them. Ya gotta start thinking that way.
I know that now. I've been trying not to get involved in anything else shady.
I got a letter for ya. From yer pa.
What? My father wrote to me?
Yep, and yer ma insisted that I hand-deliver it to you. Seems the both of 'em are worried about ya.
I'm sorry, but if it's from my father, I can't accept it.
Why not?
Obviously, he's either disowning me with that letter, or he's ordering me home. Either way, I don't want to read it.
Well, it's no use to me. Just take it.
I don't want it! My father never listened to me. So why should I listen to him!?
I should've figured you for a typical adult. I have to go!
Not so fast, Masao!
No, not you guys...
Yep⑬us guys. You're a slippery one, Masao.
You didn't seriously think you could get away, did you? Cough up the 300,000.
There's no way I can come up with that money! How do you expect me to pay?
We gave you a job, and this is how you thank us? Is that what they teach you rubes in the boonies?
Listen, you thief, it's not our problem how you come up with the money. Ask Mommy for help, sell an organ, whatever!
You need to make this right! You're in the real world now!
I don't have anything!
Gettin' a pretty decent life lesson here, eh?
On the other hand, these boys are gettin' a little carried away. They need some learnin', too.
Who do you think you are, old man?
Oh, screw this! Let's teach them both a lesson!
(That's Yamori-san!)
(What's he holding? A knife!?)

(Was he serious about that whole bank robbery thing? I'd
better stop him before this gets out of hand!)
Wha... Where am I?
Good, you're back with us, Yamori-san.
Let go of me! I can stand on my own!
I don't want your help!
You'd rather die?

Damn straight! Like I could ever accept help from the guy I
screwed over! I won't do it!
My pride won't let me!
Heh. Pretty cheap pride, if you ask me.
What's that!?
The way you put your convictions before your life is admirable.

But instead of worrying about your pride, how about worrying
about your family's future?

All the money in the world won't mean anything to your wife
if you're dead. I can't see Eri wanting that, can you?
Akiyama... You knew?
Yeah. Eri dumped me after I lost my job.

Then she started seeing you. You two got married, and she
quit working.

Losing her essentially meant losing all I had. At that
point, I was free to do just about anything.

But you have a family. It's far too early for you to say
they'd be better off without you.

What you should be doing is protecting your family's future,
even if it means eating crow meat from here on out.
You talk about having pride. Have pride in that!
Akiyama...

You're welcome to betray me. But don't ever lose sight of
what really matters.

Heh. You're right. Though I said I was doing it for my
family, I was really thinking only of myself.
Yamori-san...
To hell with my pride. Think you can offer me a loan?
Absolutely. That's what I do.

That said, you may have heard the rumors, but you'll have
to pass the test I give you.
What do I have to do?
Heh... Actually, I was going to tell you to get a divorce.

But after watching you lay your life on the line, I felt
stupid for thinking up a test that so clearly had sprung
from jealousy.

So, I'm going to offer you a loan on one condition. You
turned me down before, but I'll ask you once more.

Yamori-san, can we finally put the past behind us? Water
under the bridge? That's all I want.
Akiyama, you...
Thank you! And I'm sorry!
Man, I must be getting soft... Forgiving an act of betrayal like that.
Hana-chan won't be too happy about this...
What the fuck do ya think you're doin'!?
Shut up! It's your fault for not loaning me money!
Yamori-san!
Akiyama!?
This is crazy! You have to stop!
Stay out of this! There's no other way!
Now, take this knife and kill me.
Wha⑬?

I have life insurance. If I'm dead, my wife and kids won't
have to go hungry. Everything will be squared away!
You outta your flippin' mind!?
Come on, hurry! They won't pay out on a suicide!
*pant* *pant*
Huh? Ain't I seen you before...?
That's it! You're that Sky Finance guy from Tokyo, ain't ya?

Ah, I get it now. You're usin' this psycho to get the police
involved, so you can swoop in and take over!
The hell gave you that idea!?

You think you can pull this shit on our turf? All right,
fine! You wanna die so badly, we'll be happy to help!
Not really one for listening, are you, pal?

Come on, you two! Let's teach this greasy little shit what
happens when he fucks with us!
Hello. I'm Haruka Sawamura. It's very nice to meet you.
Welcome to Ryukyu Travel Publishing. I am Yara.
Oh, are you from Okinawa?
Born and raised. Haha! You could tell from my name?
Yes. Now I feel like I'm back home!
That's great. Heheh. It'll make for an excellent interview, don't you think?
It certainly will.
We wanted to make this unique, so we asked Okinawan children to write to you letters for the magazine.
The response was overwhelming! The greatest volume of mail we've ever received, in fact. You must be quite the celebrity there.
Really? That's amazing!
Space for the article is limited, so we picked just three letters.
I'll read them to you, and then you can comment. Sound good?
Absolutely.
All right. The first letter is from a sixth grade boy named "Professor Cosmos."
That's a pen name, I assume.
Yes, all three letters are written under pen names. I guess "Professor Cosmos" is a big fan of outer space, huh?
Anyway, here we go. "Dear Sawamura-san, I saw you dancing on TV. Wow! You're so cool!"
"I'm not athletic like you. I can't do even one pull-up, and the other kids make fun of me. What should I do?"
Heh, I had the same problem when I was a kid. So! Any advice for "Professor Cosmos"?
I would tell him... that I'm so sorry the other kids tease him! But why not turn those hurt feelings into inspiration?
He said he liked my dancing. Well, when I first started, I couldn't dance well at all. It took so much practice.
My dance coach would probably say that I'm still not good enough, even now!
But the important thing is to learn something new, and just feel good about that. So my advice is to keep trying!
Very wise. I think Professor Cosmos will be encouraged by that.
I would tell him... that I'm so sorry the other kids tease him! And if athletics aren't his thing, maybe he shouldn't worry about what they say.
After all, from the sound of his pen name he likes outer space. Why not focus on that instead?
Who cares about doing a pull-up when you can impress the other kids with your knowledge of space!
Very smart thinking. I think Professor Cosmos will be encouraged by that.
I would tell him... that I'm so sorry the other kids tease him! They probably don't realize how awful it feels.
So why not teach them a lesson? Find something about them to pick on, and make fun of them right back.
Once they know how much it hurts, maybe they'll think twice before they do it again.
...Yikes. That was a tad harsh. I hope you don't mind if I soften that up a bit for the article.
Oh! I'm sorry! Do whatever you think best.
Now, then. On to letter number two. This is from "I Heart Riona," a middle school boy.
Haha! Yeah, that pen name caught me by surprise, too. What a romantic fellow.
(An Okinawa boy with a crush on a girl named Riona? Could it be Mitsuo?)
(And Professor Cosmos said he was in sixth grade. Could that... possibly be Shiro?)
Sawamura-san?
Oh! Sorry!
(Oops! I better focus!)
Here's what it says.
"Dear Haruka, I've been watching you on TV and rooting for you! But I kind of get jealous of everyone else on TV... They're all so good-looking!"
"There's a girl I like, but I don't think she likes me. Do you think it's because I'm not very handsome?"
He's rooting for you! Must be a big fan.
Haha. He sounds like a passionate guy. As for his romantic dilemma...
Sure, looks are a big part of what first attracts us to a person.
The entertainment industry certainly puts an emphasis on looks, that's for sure.
But they aren't the only thing. When a person truly likes someone, it has much more to do with personality, I think.
For example, how kind the person is, or how trustworthy. Character can play a bigger role than appearance.
Even in the entertainment industry, it counts for something if you're attractive on the inside as well as the outside.
What I'm trying to say is... if you really like this girl, show her the quality of your character, and see what happens. Good luck!
That's very nice. I'm sure your words will mean a lot to "I Heart Riona."
Well, looks are a big part of what first attracts us to a person.
He could try putting some extra effort into his appearance.
Here in the entertainment industry, hair, makeup, and clothes are used to transform people beyond recognition.
And the really interesting thing is that people who look good start to gain confidence, and it shows.
When I'm all dressed up, I have to confess I feel different. It gives me courage when I'm onstage.
If you don't think you're very handsome, you don't have to just accept it. You can put effort into changing that.
That's great insight, coming from an entertainer. I think he'll be encouraged!
If this girl doesn't recognize the quality of your character, then you should just forget about her.
Ouch. A straight knife to the kid's heart. I hope you don't mind if I soften that up a little bit for the article.
Now for the third and final letter. It's from "Dragon Mask Man," a boy in his second year of middle school.
Uh, is there something wrong?
Oh. No, it's nothing. I misheard you. I'm sorry!
("Dragon Mask"? That has to be Taichi! All three of these letters are from Morning Glory, for sure!)
(Now I see why Ayako told me to do a good job at this interview!)
Um, are you ready to continue?
Oh! Yes, please. My apologies.
"How do you do, Sawamura-san? I always watch you when you're on TV. You're the main topic of conversation at our house!"
"We used to have people who were like a mother and father to us, but they both left on long journeys."
"Now I'm the oldest boy, so I've been trying to be responsible and dependable like they were, but it's not easy."
"What can I do to become more like them?"
Wow. He sounds like a very mature and thoughtful young man, wise beyond his years. Any advice for him, Sawamura-san?
It sounds like you've been doing great. Just keep at it.
I'm sure all the younger children look up to you... because you already have those virtues you admire in the two people who left.
Besides, those two weren't perfect. They made all kinds of mistakes.
So don't worry about what you can't do now. You're already helping your family a lot.
Wow, Sawamura-san.
Oh! I'm sorry! I...
No, please don't apologize. I think... I think "Dragon Mask Man" really needed to hear something like that. We'll print it exactly the way you said it⑬no edits.
